newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks rise on Dow record, gold bounce.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks rise on Dow record, gold bounce.

text.p: *Shares rise on new Dow record and bounce in gold price.
News Corp sale of PMP stake boosts trade. Vol 151.93 million, value A$426.28 million, 586 stocks traded, 178 steady, 310 up, 98 down.

Australian shares opened firmer on Wednesday after a fresh record on Wall Street and firm buying in gold shares after small bounce in bullion price. Trade boosted by News Corp sale in magazine unit PMP Communications.

At 10.25 a.m. (0025 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 12.2 points up at 2,691.4, while September share price index futures contracts was 13 points higher at 2,718, a 26.6 point premium to the underlying index.
Brokers said investors were starting to buy shares at the lower price after four days of price falls led by the battered gold price after the RBA sale of most of its gold holding.

"The whole market looks good. There are few bargain hunters in there, as there was a bit of panic selling yesterday," said Gordon Furner, an institutional dealer at ABN AMRO Hoare Govett. Furner said gold stocks were in demand as investors took some confidence in the slight bounce to the bullion price offshore. COMEX August gold ended up US$2.00 at $321.00 an ounce, after hitting a low of $314.60 on Monday.
"Gold stocks are looking a lot better," Furner said.
Acacia Resources, Normandy Mining and Lihir Gold were all among the most actively traded stocks, with each priced higher than Tuesday's close.

However, PMP Communications topped the turnover list when Rupert Murdoch's News Corp sold its 40 percent stake in the magazine group for A$3.20 a share. The latest trade was at A$3.13, a 14.25 percent fall on Tuesday's close.
Traders said the PMP sale was through Were Stockbroking and raised around A$320 million for News Corp.
Banks were also firmer as Australian 10-year bond futures contracts were near three-and-a-half year highs.
The bond market has factored in another rate cut by Australia's central bank. Thursday's June labour force data is seen as a key factor to determining future interest rates.
In the Australian bond market interest remained light ahead of Thursday's job data. At 11.00 a.m. (0100 GMT), the 10-year T-bond was three percentage points lower at 6.74 percent.

At the same time, the Australian dollar rallied from 18 month lows, but analysts note rally stopped well short of a recovery and trend stays down. At 11.00 a.m. (0100 GMT), the local dollar was trading at U$0.7452/57, compared with a $0.7418/23 finish here on Tuesday.
